title: a resource released twice because the owner forgot it only after the release returned
live_proof: inspection of REL_17_5 src/backend/utils/resowner/resowner.c: ResourceOwnerReleaseAll calls kind->ReleaseResource(value) and only then nitems--, writing the count back after the loop; and ResourceOwnerReleaseInternal sets owner->releasing once and never clears it, so a second entry skips the sort and still runs ResourceOwnerReleaseAll over an array that still holds the item. Quoted in PROVENANCE.md. Nothing is reverted to reproduce it
object: the resource's payload -- a libc allocation, as pgcrypto's EVP_CIPHER_CTX is
lifetime_ender: the kind's ReleaseResource frees the payload; the item is still in the owner, so abort cleanup runs ReleaseResource on it again
shape: double release through an item the owner never forgot
allocator_layer: libc (the payload); resowner's own bookkeeping is aset
nested_why: The object freed twice is a libc allocation, so both frees are events the system allocator sees. resowner.c allocates its OWN arrays out of a memory context, but those are not the object the defect frees. This is the corpus's point: the temporal, non-nested cell that mmgr-repros cannot fill.
fidelity: real subject, model resource kind: resowner.c and the seven memory managers are compiled unmodified from the pin; what the case supplies is a ResourceOwnerDesc and a payload, which is what every consumer of resowner.c supplies
memory_error_is_the_defect_why: The defect IS the second free. There is no later stale read to probe, so the invalid operation and the detection site are the same instruction.
fault_sites_why: the second free is the invalid operation, and it is made in one labelled frame so a fault can be attributed to the defect rather than to the sequence

native-detect.oracle: build-host.sh: the control must complete, then the defect run must either exit 0 having released one payload twice, or be killed with a host-allocator double-free diagnostic. glibc's tcache check is a real detection here and not a restatement, because the payload is a libc object
native-detect.verdict_note: released twice ([ReleaseThing] pass 1 then pass 2 on one address), then glibc: "free(): double free detected in tcache 2", SIGABRT exit 134; the -DRO_NEGATIVE_CONTROL build completed exit 0

host-asan.oracle: the same program under -fsanitize=address: ASan must report attempting double-free, with the report's frame in ro_free_probe
host-asan.verdict_note: AddressSanitizer: attempting double-free; #1 ro_free_probe shared/driver.c:57, #2 ReleaseThing case.c:39

status: built and reproduced on the host (native-detect, host-asan); no capability arm has been run
